# Modern (Mac) key preset

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-shortcuts.py from app/editor/keymap-presets.js (MODERN, MODERN_WHY). Do not edit by hand. -->

A profile for people who live in modern Mac apps (Figma, Linear, Xcode, Safari, VS Code) rather than in Altium. Choose **Modern (Mac)** in Preferences › Keyboard › Key preset or under Learn on the start page.

## Design

- **File and edit commands** use the familiar Mac shortcuts, including ⌘S for Save, ⇧⌘S for Save As, ⌘Z for Undo and ⇧⌘Z for Redo.
- **⌘K and ⇧⌘P open the command palette.** ⌘K also begins two-step shortcuts such as ⌘K, ⌘T. Once the palette opens, press Command with the next key to complete the shortcut, or type to search.
- **One letter per tool, as in Figma** (V select, H hand, R route, W wire, P place, N net label, T text, M measure, L layers, C comment). Hold **Space** to pan in any tool. The letters show in menus, toolbar tooltips and the cheat sheet (⌘?), whose *Single keys* group lists them first.
- **No two-key Altium sequences.** What Altium puts on P …, T …, D … sequences is on a letter, a ⌘ chord, a ⌘K chord, a menu or the palette.
- **Nothing macOS keeps for itself** (the list under *Left off* below; tests/editor/keymap.cjs checks every key of every binding against it). No ⌘ arrows either: on a PC they would be Ctrl arrows, which macOS uses for Spaces.
- **On Windows and Linux, Ctrl stands in for ⌘** (`Mod`), so the preset works there unchanged; it is not Mac-only. Ctrl+` (console) stays on Control everywhere because ⌘` cycles windows on macOS. Alt+letter (align) may open a menu on a Windows host with native menu mnemonics; Waffle's web menus have none.
- **Context, not modes.** One key can mean two things only in contexts that never overlap: R routes, but rotates while you place or move a part; V selects, but adds a via while routing; arrows nudge a selection, step the cursor while placing and pan otherwise. The preset has no conflicts on PC or Mac (tests/editor/keymap.cjs).

Module commands keep their own keys, except that Interactive Bus Routing moves from `P` `M` to `Shift+B` and the room sequences (`D` `M` …) and the library editors' `T` … sequences are cleared, and the Library panel moves to `Mod+Alt+P`; all stay on their menus. Preferences… keeps ⌘,. Ask AI about Selection uses `Mod+Alt+Shift+I` so the Properties panel keeps `Mod+Alt+I`.

## Left off on purpose

| Key | Why |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘H, ⌥⌘H | macOS: Hide Waffle, Hide Others. |
| ⌘M, ⌥⌘M | macOS: Minimize, Minimize All. |
| ⌘Q, ⇧⌘Q, ⌃⌘Q | Quit, Log Out, Lock Screen. |
| ⌘⇥, ⌘` | App and window cycling. |
| ⌘Space, ⌃⌘Space, ⌥⌘Space | Spotlight, the emoji viewer, Finder search. |
| ⌃⌘F | Full screen (the native View menu). |
| ⌥⌘⎋, ⇧⌘⎋ | Force Quit; Waffle's Pause All Extensions kill switch. |
| ⇧⌘3, ⇧⌘4, ⇧⌘5 | Screenshots. |
| ⌥⌘D | Show or hide the Dock. |
| ⌃←, ⌃→, ⌃↑, ⌃↓ | Mission Control and Spaces. (So nothing uses ⌘ arrows either: on a PC they would be Ctrl arrows.) |
| F-keys | Mac keyboards make them media keys; the Allegro-like preset is the function-key profile. |
| Two-key Altium sequences (P W, T D …) | The point of this preset; rare commands are ⌘K chords or the palette instead. |
| ⌘1…⌘9 selection memory, J 1…9 saved views | ⌘1…⌘9 are document tabs here. Selection memory and saved views stay on Window › Selection Memory and the palette. |
| ⌘G Find Next | Waffle's find opens a list; there is no incremental find to repeat, so ⌘G groups as in Figma. |
| ⇧⌘1 / ⇧1 zoom to fit (Figma) | Shift+digit types a different character on each layout; ⌘0 fits. |
| F2 rename | Return renames, as in Finder. |
| Ctrl+W route, Ctrl+M measure, Ctrl+H select net | Altium-isms on Control; R, M and the palette replace them. |

Never bound (checked by tests/editor/keymap.cjs): `Meta+H`, `Alt+Meta+H`, `Meta+M`, `Alt+Meta+M`, `Meta+Q`, `Shift+Meta+Q`, `Ctrl+Meta+Q`, `Meta+Tab`, `Shift+Meta+Tab`, `Meta+Space`, `Ctrl+Meta+Space`, `Alt+Meta+Space`, `Ctrl+Meta+F`, `Alt+Meta+Escape`, `Shift+Meta+Escape`, `Meta+``, `Shift+Meta+``, `Shift+Meta+3`, `Shift+Meta+4`, `Shift+Meta+5`, `Alt+Meta+D`, `Ctrl+Left`, `Ctrl+Right`, `Ctrl+Up`, `Ctrl+Down`, `F11`.
